camera.label: Theatrical
camera.description: Playful theatrical art-rock coverage: low wide-angle performance masters, face-forward close-ups, Dutch tilts, whip-pans, tracking, circling, and overhead views, with tender held portraits for quieter passages.
camera.guidance: Build a cheeky, theatrical performance through strong contrasts between low wide-angle masters, waist-up action, and wide-angle close-ups with the face large and expressive in frame. Let foreground hands, existing props, and softly blurred background activity add depth around the principal performer. Use purposeful whip-pans, backward tracking ahead of a moving performer, side tracking, and circling coverage for energetic passages; use held mirror portraits and a slow medium-to-close push-in for intimate passages. Match each choice to the scene's existing action, musical energy, and available duration. Place cuts on the supplied shot plan and performance beats. Across cuts, preserve each person's established position, orientation, posture, held objects, and ongoing action as the camera changes angle and framing. Keep facial expressions readable during vocal cues. Use the project's mapped subjects, locations, and props, adapting the camera setup to their actual staging. A held composition can carry a big gesture or a final pose; camera movement serves the performance.

performance.label: Theatrical
performance.direction: Use playful theatrical art-rock performance with cheeky confidence, comic timing, and bold readable physical acting. Match gestures to the lyric or story beat: a purposeful strut, cocked hip, exaggerated prim posture, mock bow or curtsy, rhythmic stomp, shoulder bounce, playful spin, or a knowing gesture toward the lens. Choose actions that fit the scene's staging, available time, and existing props. Let interactions play as clear setup-and-reaction beats, with supporting performers reacting in character and instrumentalists moving in time with their parts. Shape assigned vocal delivery with sly, teasing, mock-regal, gleeful, defiant, or triumphant intent as the words require; quieter passages settle into tender stillness, small gestures, and fond warmth. Preserve the supplied words, assigned performers, vocal windows, and ongoing physical action across shots. Scale each gesture to the framing so the face and the performance remain readable.

facial.label: Theatrical
facial.description: Big, cheeky expressions with comic timing and tender quieter beats
facial.direction: Use big, playful, cheeky facial acting that develops from beat to beat. Select expressive details that fit the words and each character's role: brows shooting up, one eyebrow cocked, sly sideways glances, eyes widening with mock alarm or flaring with glee, extravagant eye rolls, wide grins, slow knowing winks, mock-innocent pouts, and sugary fake-polite smiles that crack into delight. Connect each change to a specific thought, gesture, lyric, or reaction, giving each expression time to read clearly. Let a supporting character's prim disapproval, frozen astonishment, skeptical raised brow, or deadpan pride develop into amusement when the scene calls for it. For intimate passages, soften the eyes and cheeks, lift the inner brows gently, and settle into a small fond smile and warm knowing gaze. Keep assigned vocal articulation aligned to its supplied cue windows, with natural expressive resting mouth shapes between cues and occasional natural blinks.
